elements.element: Customer may terminate Vendor for convenience, without cause.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2A permits the Issuer to terminate the Servicer's rights and obligations “for convenience, in whole or in part, at any time and without cause.”

elements.element: Customer's termination for convenience may become effective on thirty (30) days' prior written notice.
elements.evidence: Although Section 7.2A specifies thirty days' prior written notice, termination cannot become effective before a Successor Servicer accepts its engagement. Because that event has no deadline, the operative language does not guarantee termination after 30 days.

elements.element: Customer receives a pro-rata refund of fees prepaid for periods after the effective termination date.
elements.evidence: The Servicer must refund “any amounts prepaid in respect of the period after such effective date,” which provides the required time-based refund of unearned prepaid amounts.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 7.1 prohibits the Servicer from resigning unless it determines that it is legally unable to perform. Neither Section 7.2A nor Section 8.3 grants the Servicer a convenience-termination right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate Vendor for convenience, without cause.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2A expressly grants the Issuer a right to terminate the Servicer for convenience and without cause.

elements.element: Customer's termination for convenience may become effective on 60–90 days' prior written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause states a 30-day notice period, not a period within the required 60–90-day range, and effectiveness may be delayed indefinitely pending acceptance by a Successor Servicer.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2A states that no termination fee, penalty, or other compensation is payable, other than accrued and unpaid fees for services already performed. A zero early-termination fee is below the three-month cap.

elements.element: Vendor has a right to terminate for convenience.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause grants no convenience-termination right to the Servicer; Section 7.1 instead prohibits resignation except where the Servicer is legally unable to perform.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination for convenience may become effective only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The Servicer has no termination-for-convenience right at all, so there is no permitted mid-term Vendor convenience termination; the restriction is satisfied by the broader prohibition.

elements.element: Vendor must provide ninety (90) days' prior notice to exercise any termination-for-convenience right.
elements.evidence: No Vendor termination-for-convenience right exists, so the condition triggering this notice requirement is demonstrably absent. Section 7.1 permits resignation only for legal inability, not convenience.

result.reason: The redline nominally grants the Issuer a 30-day convenience-termination right, a refund of unearned prepaid amounts, and no termination fee. However, effectiveness is conditioned on a Successor Servicer accepting engagement, with no deadline, so the Issuer is not assured an effective exit after 30 days. The fallback is also not fully met because the Customer notice period is outside the specified 60–90-day range and the Servicer is not granted the contemplated end-of-term termination right. The redline is not minimal and does not preserve unrelated commercial terms because it also adds an unrelated waiver-of-Servicer-Termination-Events provision. Drafting is further weakened by the uncapped successor condition, the misplaced Section 7.2A after Section 8.3, and the retained incomplete sentence “The Issuer will.”
